purpose: Pre-execution deterministic saturation and physical-retirement experiment
authority: Implementation experiment declaration; no product or platform acceptance

workload.mode: offline controlled DecisionModel with explicit non-cooperative native completion gates

method: Admit eight distinct edits and hold each physical provider callback. Admit one saturated edit, interrupt the first round, record whether a canonical settlement arrives while physical work is held, release exactly that request, and admit a tenth edit that reuses the settled permit. Start shutdown with eight physical requests held, observe it for 25ms, then release every callback and await shutdown. Measure admission/Stop/saturation latency, release-to-shutdown completion, event-loop delay, logical retained bytes, RSS and simultaneous physical effects. Gates bound ordering, not provider response time.
requiredInvariants: Exactly eight simultaneous physical requests reached
Saturated edit does not start a ninth request
Round interruption does not settle a held physical request
Permit reuse follows physical and canonical settlement
Shutdown remains pending while physical requests are held
Shutdown does not finish before physical completion
All physical callbacks and canonical request permits settle before final accounting clears
comparisonRule: Use the unchanged ratio and absolute allowances from benchmark-contract.json against this workload baseline. A baseline shutdown that finishes before physical completion is invalid for shutdown latency comparison; report that fact and leave that comparative metric unproven rather than treating premature completion as a faster valid baseline.
limitations: Synthetic offline physical callbacks only; no real Jev transport, wire cancellation, live host or cross-platform support evidence.
